[session compacted: the 124 earliest messages were replaced by the summary below; the 174 most recent messages after it are verbatim.]

---

## Work

Issue #460 (sub-issue of #441, §5): make the aggregation dispatch **fail-closed** — pass the already-written `atomaton:aggregated` marker to `dispatchRunner` as its `markerCommentId`, make that comment carry the dispatch tag (so it is one comment = marker + ask), and close the hole where a failed marker POST still let the dispatch go out.

Repo `yuma-seno/atomaton`, workdir `/home/runner/work/atomaton/atomaton`, branch `main` at `884da10`. Role `engineer`; this run was started by the `atomaton` agent.

## Decided (and why)

- **One comment per completion.** The gate already posts the marker; the dispatch posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Passing `markerCommentId` deletes that second POST, and the marker must therefore carry `DISPATCH_TAG`, because `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only when the ask is a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch` — otherwise it posts a separate claim, i.e. two new comments again.
- **Fail-closed rule in `refuseOutstandingRequest`:** when there is no marker, a dispatch that names **no ask of its own** is refused (`unconfirmed`); a dispatch that **does** name one (the runner hand-off's result comment, which its run claims) still goes out with the ordering check skipped. This keeps hand-offs working while stopping a run nothing on the thread accounts for.
- **No double DELETE.** `dispatchRunner`'s own `removeMarker` already deletes a caller-supplied marker on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. So `aggregation.ts` must NOT call `takeBackMarker` for those two (a second DELETE answers 404 and would be logged as "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry" — the opposite of what happened). `unconfirmed` maps to `dispatch-failed` there with no DELETE.
- **Empty agent ⇒ no dispatch tag**, since `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader; the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.
- `dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording was widened: it now covers both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible", instead of claiming GitHub hid the machinery's own marker.

## Done (all typecheck-clean)

**`src/adapters/actions/dispatch.ts`** — new `refuseUnconfirmed(d, why)` helper (logs, posts the notice, returns `"unconfirmed"`); `refuseOutstandingRequest` now refuses when `markerId === undefined` **and** `d.ask` is empty; doc comments on `postDispatchMarker`, `DispatchOutcome`'s `unconfirmed`, and the function updated.

**`src/app/aggregation.ts`** — imports `DISPATCH_TAG`; `const agent = parentAgent(...)` hoisted; marker body is `DISPATCH_TAG.write(agent)` (omitted when empty) + `AGGREGATED_TAG.write(closedNum)` + the prose line; `dispatchRunner` receives `markerCommentId: markerId` and `agent`; outcome mapping rewritten with comments explaining the split.

**`src/domain/work/closed-target.ts`** — `dispatchUnconfirmedNotice` doc + body widened.

**Tests** — `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts`: new `describe("the dispatch's own evidence")` with `runMarkerless({target, ask?})`; two tests (POST fails → `unconfirmed`, no `workflow` call, notice posted; caller-supplied ask → `dispatched` with `ask=900`).
`src/app/aggregation.test.ts`: `thread()` now appends a **neutral** entry `{id: MARKER_ID=777, body: "a comment with no tag on it"}` (neutral so it can't trigger `already-aggregated`); `PARKED` = `<!-- atomaton:ended=waiting answers=0 run=0 -->` added to `PARENT_AGENT` (necessary: the pre-existing dispatch marker is otherwise the newest event → `parent-busy`); `DISPATCH_MARKER` const deleted and its spreads removed; two new tests — "an aggregation posts exactly one comment, and it is both the marker and the ask" and "a dispatch the thread cannot confirm is not sent, and the marker comes back" (15 s timeout).
`src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts`: first test rewritten to one POST rule (`atomaton:aggregated` → `556`), a thread fixture with the marker id 556 plus a `waiting` ending, and an assertion of exactly one write carrying both tags.

**Verified so far:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test ./src/app/aggregation.test.ts` 20 pass; `bun test ./src/adapters/actions` 24 pass; `bun test ./src/adapters ./src/app ./src/entrypoints/machinery` 699 pass; `dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` 3 pass. Full `bun test` gave 2113 pass / 76 fail — **every failure is a generated-workflow/dist artifact test** failing because `dist/` did not exist; `bun run synth` was then run successfully and only the six `src/` files are modified (`dist/**` is gitignored, `git status` confirms).

## Still open

1. Re-run the full suite now that `bun run synth` has produced `dist/`, to confirm the 76 generated-workflow failures are gone (they were an artefact of a missing build output, not of this change — but this must be **measured**, not assumed).
2. `commit_and_push(message=...)` — nothing is committed yet; the worktree is discarded when the run ends.
3. `create_pr(title, body, reviewer="reviewer")`, body carrying the behaviour and the verification results. Then read `validation_dispatched`; if `false`, say so (nothing was scheduled) as the last useful thing.

## Must not

- Bump `version` in `package.json`, or release.
- Edit `dist/**` or `.github/**` (generated / self-deploy only); `.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/*.ts` is a copy of the old release and must stay untouched.
- Break the answers-request path: `answersRequest` dispatches post no marker and must keep going out (all existing tests unchanged and green).
- Add the double `DELETE` back in `aggregation.ts` for `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`.
- Put atomaton issue numbers (`#NNN`) into `docs/`.
- `create_root_issue` vs `create_sub_issue`: no tool-degradation report was encountered this run, so nothing to file.

Now let me plan the implementation.

Current state:
- `aggregation.ts:332-342` writes the aggregation marker with `commentOnWithId`, fail-closed if null.
- `aggregation.ts:344-352` calls dispatchRunner without `markerCommentId` and without `ask`.
- dispatchRunner: when no `answersRequest` and no `markerCommentId`, it posts its own marker (`postDispatchMarker`); if the POST fails -> `undefined` -> `refuseOutstandingRequest` returns `undefined` -> dispatch proceeds. That's the hole.
- With `markerCommentId` provided: `markerId = provided`, `refuseOutstandingRequest(d, markerId, ownMarker=false)` runs the freshness probe on that comment. Marker not visible -> for ownMarker=false, no repost; deletes marker (`removeMarker()`) — which would DELETE the caller's aggregation marker. That's the take-back question in scope item 4.

Important: for the aggregation path, the aggregation marker is the caller's comment. If `refuseOutstandingRequest` returns `refused-outstanding` or `unconfirmed`, marker is DELETEd by dispatch.ts. Then `aggregation.ts`'s `takeBackMarker` would DELETE again (harmless 404) for `refused-outstanding`. Hmm, double delete: dispatch.ts deletes marker on refusal, then aggregation deletes it again in `takeBackMarker`. For aggregation's `refused-outstanding` branch it calls `takeBackMarker(why)` which does DELETE again — idempotent-ish (404 errors logged as "marker could not be removed" — misleading!). That would produce a misleading log and the `describeGateResult` claims. We need to handle this cleanly.

Let me think about the design carefully.

Scope items:
1. Pass `markerCommentId: markerId` from aggregation.ts's dispatchRunner call. Then postDispatchMarker doesn't run for this path.
2. The adopted aggregation marker must be readable by the freshness probe: `checkDispatchMarker` reads the comment listing and only checks the id is visible; it doesn't read the dispatch tag. Wait — item 2 says "adopting marker must be in a shape the freshness probe can read, i.e. carries the dispatch tag". Let me recheck `checkDispatchMarker`: it just checks the id is in the listing. It doesn't read the tag. Hmm. But other readers do: `shapedThread`/`requestOutstanding` reads `isDispatchMarker` on bodies. Wait — in `checkDispatchMarker`, the marker is EXCLUDED from entries, so its dispatch-ness isn't needed for that call.

But other things read the marker:
- `claim_turn.ts`: `isMarker = !human && DISPATCH_TAG.hasProse(body)` — if the ask comment is the marker with the dispatch tag, the claim is appended in place (PATCH) rather than posting a second comment. If it's NOT a marker, claim_turn posts a separate claim comment. Both work, but the acceptance criterion says "集約による dispatch のたびにスレッドに新規投稿されるコメントは 1 件(集約マーカー)で、それが dispatch タグと ask を兼ねる。第 2 の marker コメントは投稿されない。" So the aggregation marker should carry the dispatch tag so that claim_turn appends in place — avoiding a second comment posted at run start. Yes, that's the point: the dispatch tag on the aggregation marker means the runner claims it in place (one comment).
- Also `aggregation.ts`'s own idempotency read uses AGGREGATED_TAG on bodies; adding a dispatch tag doesn't affect that.
- But careful: does adding a dispatch tag to the aggregation marker affect `requestOutstanding` reads elsewhere? The marker is the machinery's own ask, which is exactly right: an aggregation marker with the dispatch tag reads as "asked" — like other markers. Actually the current aggregation marker, past dispatch, is followed by the dispatch marker comment ("Atomaton: X starting on this issue") which is the "asked" event. With the adoption, the aggregation marker carries the dispatch tag and thus becomes the asked event. That preserves behaviour: outstanding request if not claimed.

Hmm, but is it negative? In `aggregation.ts`'s `dispatchOrchestratorIfReady`, the idempotency read is `AGGREGATED_TAG.readProse(body) === closedNum`. Adding DISPATCH_TAG doesn't change it.

Also `mostRecentAgentOn` reads `parseCommentCommand(proseOnly(body)).agent` — does `parseCommentCommand` read the `atomaton:dispatch=NAME` tag? Yes! comment-command.ts parses the dispatch form. So a marker carrying `atomaton:dispatch=atomaton` also names the agent. That means `parentAgent()` could pick it up. But careful: in aggregation.ts, `parentAgent` is computed at line 346 — AFTER the marker was written at 332. The marker body carries `atomaton:dispatch=<agent>`; if `agent` is the agent we're dispatching, then `mostRecentAgentOn` would return it. But we read the agent BEFORE writing the marker? Let's see: `parentAgent(opts.repo, opts.parent)` is called inside the dispatchRunner call arguments, which is evaluated after the marker write (line 332) and before/inside dispatchRunner. The marker write happens at :332, then at :346 `agent: parentAgent(...)` reads the thread. If the marker is visible in the read, and it carries `atomaton:dispatch=<agent>`, the answer would be self-referential: we need to know the agent to write the tag, but we learn the agent by reading the thread. Circular!

So: we must read the agent BEFORE writing the marker, and then write the marker with the dispatch tag naming that agent. That is a natural reordering: read agent → write marker (carrying AGGREGATED + DISPATCH=agent) → dispatch with markerCommentId. If the agent is empty, we can still write the marker with no dispatch tag? Hmm, dispatchRunner refuses empty agent -> `failed` -> take-back deletes the marker. Existing test "a parent that names no agent is not dispatched onto with an empty name" expects `dispatch-failed` and marker written then deleted (the test "a failed dispatch takes the aggregation marker back" uses NAMES_NOBODY). Actually wait: in the current code, marker is written before the agent read. If we move the agent read before the write, then for NAMES_NOBODY the agent is "" and we write a marker with just AGGREGATED (no dispatch tag), then dispatchRunner refuses with "failed", then takeBackMarker deletes it. The test asserts DELETE comments/777 -> still passes. Ok.

But should we write the marker at all if the agent is empty? Yes — keep behaviour: the marker write is the idempotency claim, and the take-back on failure re-enables retry. Alternatively we could not write and return... but that changes tests. Keep simple: read agent first (may be ""), write marker with dispatch tag when agent non-empty, dispatch.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety about ordering that matters for correctness: currently the agent is read after the marker write. If the read is bad... doesn't matter. Moving it earlier: the agent read is from the same thread listing — `mostRecentAgentOn` → `commentBodies` → `listComments`. Both reads happen anyway.

Now item 3: close the hole in `dispatch.ts:447`. The rule: refuse when neither caller-provided marker/ask exists AND the marker POST failed. Precisely: `refuseOutstandingRequest(d, markerId, ownMarker)` — when `markerId === undefined`, that means `postDispatchMarker` failed (since provided "" means post failed or none given). So: if markerId undefined → the dispatch has no evidence on the thread; we must not dispatch. What outcome? There are options:
- `"unconfirmed"` — semantically "the marker could not be confirmed in the thread, so the ordering check could not be trusted". A POST failure is the "post itself may have failed" case which the doc says now leads to unconfirmed. That fits and posts the `dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`. But `unconfirmed` posts a notice with "GitHub did not show the machinery its own marker in the thread" — accurate-ish for a POST failure ("could not be confirmed"). Hmm the notice text says "GitHub did not show the machinery its own marker in the thread" — for a POST failure it's "the marker could not be written". The existing notice covers "could not be confirmed". Could be acceptable, but maybe add a distinct outcome `"unconfirmed"` with a different log line, reusing the same notice. Or add a new outcome kind. Adding a new outcome value touches callers: aggregation (needs a gate result kind), dispatch_agent.ts (exit code), dispatch-targets (returns boolean), mcp tools.

Simplicity: reuse `"unconfirmed"`. Its doc says: "The dispatch marker could not be confirmed in the thread, so the ordering check could not be trusted. Nobody was dispatched, and a notice is posted. Separate from `failed`, which is GitHub rejecting the dispatch itself. This is the read side: the marker was posted but never became visible..." We'd extend the doc to include "or was never posted at all" — the outcome means "no evidence on the thread, so no dispatch". The notice `dispatchUnconfirmedNotice` says "GitHub did not show the machinery its own marker in the thread, so it could not tell whether another run had already been asked for." That is true for the POST-failure case too (the marker is not in the thread). It says "This is usually transient. Retry shortly" — reasonable for a POST failure (rate limit / 5xx).

Hmm, but wait: there's a distinction with `aggregation.ts` mapping outcomes to gate results. Currently aggregation maps `unconfirmed` (from dispatchRunner) to... let's see: `outcome === "dispatched"` → dispatched; `refused-closed` → parent-closed; `refused-outstanding` → parent-busy + takeBackMarker; anything else → takeBackMarker + dispatch-failed. So `unconfirmed` → `dispatch-failed` with take-back. Good: with adoption, `unconfirmed` means the aggregation marker isn't visible; but the aggregation marker was just written by us (commentOnWithId returned an id). Then dispatch's probe couldn't see it → unconfirmed → dispatch.ts's `removeMarker()` DELETEs it already; then aggregation's takeBackMarker deletes again → logs "AND the aggregation marker could not be removed (404...)" — misleading double work.

So I need to sort out who owns the take-back when the marker is the caller's. Item 4 in the scope: "採用したマーカーに対する take-back(`:441` の DELETE が何を消すか)を推論してコメント/テストで固定する". So: with an adopted marker, dispatch.ts's `removeMarker()` deletes the CALLER's comment. What should happen?

Consider each refusal in `refuseOutstandingRequest` with an adopted marker (ownMarker=false):
1. Read failure → removeMarker() → deletes caller's directive/aggregation marker. For the post-merge directive: the comment is the first user message of the re-invoked run; if we delete it, the run isn't started so nothing reads it. The doc on `markerCommentId` says: "A refusal removes it, as it removes a marker posted here: the directive would otherwise stay on the thread as an ask nobody took up, and no run will read it because none was started." So yes, deleting the caller's comment on refusal is the declared behaviour.
2. Marker never visible → removeMarker() (deletes the caller's comment), posts unconfirmed notice. Same rationale.
3. outstanding → removeMarker() → deletes caller's comment.

For aggregation this means: on a refusal, dispatch.ts deletes the aggregation marker. Then aggregation's take-back also tries. The aggregated marker's idempotency: if the marker is deleted, a later close can retry — which is exactly what aggregation's `takeBackMarker` wants for `dispatch-failed`/`parent-busy`. So having dispatch.ts delete it is the same end state, and aggregation's subsequent DELETE is a no-op 404 that logs a misleading line. Options:
(a) In aggregation, pass markerCommentId and let dispatch own the removal on refusal; aggregation's takeBackMarker could skip if... but aggregation cannot know whether dispatch deleted it. Hmm.
(b) Keep aggregation's takeBackMarker as the sole deleter by making dispatch NOT delete an adopted (caller-provided) marker — i.e. `removeMarker()` only deletes markers this module posted (`ownMarker`), leaving the caller's comment in place for the caller to decide. But the `markerCommentId` doc explicitly says "A refusal removes it, as it removes a marker posted here" — that's a documented decision with reasoning (directive would stay as an ask nobody took up). Changing it would change behaviour for post-merge/rejected directives — those callers do not take anything back; they rely on dispatch deleting on refusal. Breaking that would leave phantom asks. Not good.

(c) Make aggregation's take-back tolerant: it deletes and, if the DELETE fails, distinguish "already gone" from "could not remove". But that's noise.

(d) Better: have aggregation NOT take back separately when dispatch refused with a marker it already removed. How can aggregation know? The outcome tells it: `refused-outstanding` and `unconfirmed` both caused dispatch to remove the adopted marker; `failed` (GitHub rejected the dispatch call) does NOT remove it unless refusalEnding is set... let's check: in `dispatchRunner`, on `dispatchWorkflow` failure: if `d.refusalEnding !== undefined` then delete + notice. Aggregation passes no refusalEnding, so for `failed` the marker stays → aggregation's takeBackMarker removes it. But wait — `failed` also covers empty agent, which happens before marker posting (if agent empty, dispatch refuses early, nothing posted) — with adoption, the marker was posted by aggregation so it remains; aggregation's take-back removes it. Good.

So the mapping becomes:
- `dispatched` → dispatched (marker stays, claimed by the run).
- `refused-closed` → parent-closed, marker stays (no delete).
- `refused-outstanding` → parent-busy; dispatch already removed the adopted marker. aggregation must not delete again (or at least not claim it removed it).
- `unconfirmed` → dispatch-failed; dispatch already removed the marker.
- `failed` → dispatch-failed; aggregation must remove the marker itself (dispatch did not).
- `superseded` → impossible here (no answersRequest).

Hmm, that's a subtle dependency: aggregation's removal logic depends on whether dispatch deleted. That's fragile coupling between modules: "did the callee clean up my marker?" A cleaner approach: make the ownership explicit and single-owner.

Alternative cleaner design: keep the removal entirely with dispatch.ts for adopted markers (as documented), and have aggregation not delete for the outcomes where dispatch handles it. But we still need aggregation to delete on `failed`.

Alternative: have dispatch.ts NOT delete adopted markers, i.e. ownership stays with the caller, and instead the two callers that adopt directives (post-merge, rejected) delete their own on refusal. That's a bigger refactor and those callers get a boolean.

Hmm. Which is less in code? Let's think about a third option: aggregation deletes on its own for its own outcomes, and dispatch deleting an adopted marker is documented as "the refusal removes the ask it adopted so no phantom request remains". If both delete, second DELETE is a 404 that aggregation's takeBackMarker logs as a failure. We can make aggregation's takeBackMarker treat a 404/not-found as already-removed. But detecting is fiddly (error text matching).

Actually, the cleanest conceptual framing: **the take-back belongs to whoever wrote the comment.** dispatch.ts wrote neither the aggregation marker nor the directive. Deleting someone else's comment is surprising. But it *is* documented as intentional for the directive case: "A refusal removes it, as it removes a marker posted here: the directive would otherwise stay on the thread as an ask nobody took up, and no run will read it because none was started."

Hmm wait. Is that actually safe for the aggregation case? Deleting the aggregation marker on a refusal is exactly what aggregation wants (retry possible). So both want the same thing. The only issue is double-DELETE and a misleading log.

Simplest surgical approach: in aggregation, decide the take-back per outcome and state it. Since dispatch already removes the adopted marker on `refused-outstanding` and `unconfirmed`, aggregation does the removal only for `failed`. But that's implicit knowledge of dispatch internals.

Alternative that avoids the coupling: don't pass a *caller-marked* marker through the delete path — instead pass `markerCommentId` plus a new flag? No, more options is worse.

Let me reconsider: maybe the cleanest is to make the removal in dispatch.ts report *whether it removed*, and let aggregation not need to know by removing the double-delete risk: aggregation's `takeBackMarker` could first check? No.

Hmm, actually think about what happens for `refused-outstanding`: dispatch removes the marker (the aggregation marker). Then aggregation maps to `parent-busy` and its describeGateResult says "The aggregation marker was removed, so closing a sub-issue again retries it". True. So the message is right even though the deletion was done by dispatch. So the only cost is the extra DELETE call and a misleading log line "AND the aggregation marker could not be removed". We could just... let aggregation do the delete for all its needing outcomes and make the log honest by noting a 404 means it is already gone? Eh.

Better idea: **Dispatch should not delete a marker the caller provided**, and instead the caller-provided-marker contract says "the caller owns the comment; a refusal leaves it, and the caller decides". But then post-merge/rejected directives stay as phantom asks — behaviour regression for those paths. Unless... they're already claimed-and-refused understanding. Hmm no, no run starts.

OK let me weigh a different decomposition: what if aggregation does NOT pass markerCommentId, but instead passes `markerBody`/... no, scope explicitly says pass markerCommentId and remove the seed POST.

Let's just decide: **the adopted marker is removed by the refusal in dispatch.ts (existing documented contract), and aggregation's take-back handles only the outcome where dispatch did not remove it (`failed`, which is where GitHub rejected the call).** And I'll add a test for each. To keep the coupling honest and single-sourced, I can express it as: `dispatchRunner` returns an outcome; aggregation's take-back is stated as "the marker is already gone for the two outcomes where the refusal took it back; for `failed` the comment stands and this removes it". Hmm, but "the refusal takes it back" is a property of `refuseOutstandingRequest` for both own and adopted markers, and for `unconfirmed` too. That's stable enough and documented.

But careful about the `failed` path: `dispatchRunner` with `refusalEnding === undefined` does NOT delete the marker on `failed`. Aggregation passes no refusalEnding → so aggregation must delete. Good.

Yet there's a subtlety: is there any other outcome dispatch could return? `superseded` (not for us). Let's write aggregation's switch explicitly for all cases so a new outcome is a compile error? `DispatchOutcome` is a union of 6; a `switch` with exhaustiveness gives safety. But mapping to "who deletes" — I could write:

```ts
// The refusal in dispatch.ts removes the marker it adopted, with the same argument it
// posts its own: a comment left behind is a request nobody will take up. So for those
// two outcomes the marker is already gone here, and only a rejected dispatch call
// (`failed`, where the deletion above does not run) leaves it standing.
```

Hmm, is `refused-outstanding`'s removal necessary? It removes the marker, meaning the "aggregated" claim disappears → a later caller retries. That's the intended `parent-busy` semantics. Yes.

Now, wait. There's another thought: maybe it's better for dispatch.ts to NOT delete adopted markers and for aggregation to delete its own; and for directives, dispatch deletion is documented-and-wanted. Two different owners for two different callers is worse.

Alternatively: have dispatch.ts delete adopted markers (unchanged), and aggregation handles `failed` only, and add a test that exactly one DELETE of the marker happens for `parent-busy`/`unconfirmed` (pinning "no double delete, no misleading log"). I'll go with that, with a comment on the aggregation side.

Hmm, but hold on. Let me reconsider whether `unconfirmed` can even occur for the aggregation marker now: `commentOnWithId` returned an id, so the POST succeeded; visibility lag then triggers retries, reposts skipped (ownMarker=false), then `unconfirmed` → deletes the marker and posts an unconfirmed notice. Aggregation maps to `dispatch-failed` — but its describe says "The dispatch FAILED. The aggregation marker was removed, so closing a sub-issue again retries it". Accurate.

Also failure notice duplication: dispatch's `unconfirmed` posts a notice on the target, and aggregation's `withNotice` only posts for `undetermined`, so no double notice. Also aggregation's describeGateResult for dispatch-failed says "...The aggregation marker was removed..." Good.

Wait, but there's a subtle problem with the aggregation mapping `unconfirmed` → `dispatch-failed` and its commentary. Fine.

Now item 3's second half: "answers-request のように ask が caller 提供の経路は現行どおり dispatch できること". In `dispatchRunner`, with `answersRequest`, `refuseSupersededAsk` runs and no marker is posted; `ask = d.ask`. That path is untouched as long as my change is only in the `else` branch (the marker path) and specifically about `markerId === undefined`.

Also consider: should the fail-closed apply when the caller provided a marker? No — provided marker means evidence exists; if it's not visible, existing logic refuses with `unconfirmed`.

What about `d.ask` provided but no marker (non-answersRequest)? E.g. runner's hand-off passes `ask` (the result comment id) plus no markerCommentId, not answersRequest → dispatch posts its own marker; if the POST fails, `ask` is set from d.ask; the run has an ask to claim, and the evidence is the result comment. Hmm! In that case, is fail-closed right? The `ask` the caller named is itself a comment the caller wrote moments before — so there IS evidence on the thread. Refusing there would break the hand-off path (runner dispatch step passes ask=postResultCommentStep.comment_id). If the marker POST fails, the run would still have the hand-off's result comment as ask, and the ordering check... hmm, the ordering check can't run. But the *general principle* is "no dispatch without evidence" — evidence exists (the ask comment). But the ordering check can't be trusted.

Careful: this is a real behaviour-change risk. The issue says: "caller からの ask/marker も無く marker POST も失敗した場合、dispatch を実行しない". So the rule is exactly: no ask AND no marker from caller AND marker POST failed → refuse. When the caller named an `ask`, dispatch may proceed (current behaviour) — since the ask is the comment that will be claimed, and refusing would break the hand-off path.

But hmm: what does the current code do when `d.ask` is provided and marker POST fails? `markerId = undefined`, `refuseOutstandingRequest` returns undefined (skip check), `ask = d.ask ?? markerId` → d.ask. Dispatch proceeds. Should this stay? Per the issue scope: yes, "ask が caller 提供の経路は現行どおり dispatch できること" — that covers answersRequest explicitly but the rule statement says "ask/marker も無く". So keep: if `ask` present, proceed.

Now what about the marker POST failing *and* no ask: refuse. Which outcome? Let me think about `dispatch_agent.ts` — the runner's hand-off always passes ask... Actually `dispatch_agent.ts` passes `ask: (values.ask ?? "").trim() || undefined`. In the runner's dispatch step ask is set. In other callers (branches?) it may be absent. And `dispatch_sub_agent.ts` (launch_sub_agent) passes no ask and no markerCommentId → marker POST failure now refuses instead of dispatching a sub-agent. Is that a behaviour degradation? It's the fail-closed intent: "証跡なしでは dispatch しない". #441's design: "証跡無しの dispatch はしない". So yes, `launch_sub_agent` with a failed marker POST now refuses, and dispatchSubAgent throws ("could not dispatch ... see the workflow log") — which the atomaton reports per-task. That's the intent: no silent unclaimed runs. I should note it in the PR body.

What outcome name? `unconfirmed` reuses the notice and dispatch_agent's exit-1 path; aggregation maps to dispatch-failed (with no marker to take back... but aggregation's marker was provided so it IS present — hmm! Wait: if aggregation provides `markerCommentId`, then markerId is defined, so this new branch never triggers for aggregation. Right.)

Let me now decide the outcome: I'll use `"unconfirmed"`, and update its doc to cover both ways evidence can be missing (POST failed, or the marker never became visible). Log message must be distinct though: "could not post the dispatch marker on #N: <err>" (from postDispatchMarker) then a line saying nothing was dispatched. Where should that live? In `dispatchRunner`, the else-branch:

```ts
const provided = ...;
markerId = provided === "" ? postDispatchMarker(d) : provided;
const refusal = refuseOutstandingRequest(d, markerId, provided === "");
```

Hmm — if I want the fail-closed to be fail-closed, I can implement it inside `refuseOutstandingRequest`: currently `if (markerId === undefined) return undefined;` with a comment. Change to:

```ts
if (markerId === undefined) {
  // Only a marker this module posted can be missing here: a caller-provided one is
  // always a string. Its POST failing leaves the thread with nothing that says this
  // dispatch asked for anything, so the ordering check cannot run and the run it
  // started would be one no reader could account for...
  if (d.ask !== undefined && `${d.ask}`.trim() !== "") return undefined;  // evidence exists: the ask
  // refuse
}
```

The route for an agent that wants to hand a person the ball is not a label: it is
prose in the body, and the notify tag the body already carries. The labels are
applied when the run holding the node ends, by the machinery, to the node it was
holding.

An agent that does apply one by hand is not corrupting a filter, it is writing a
turn that never took place — and the machinery reads its own state wrong for as
long as the label survives. That is why the tools refuse it rather than relying on
this page.

## How a parent learns its children are done

The count that re-invokes the parent is made of the `sub-issue` label and the
dispatch marker in each child's thread, read together by `countOpenSiblings`:
the label says this issue was born a delivery task, the marker says an agent was
actually started on it. A child created as a later phase of a plan and never
launched carries no marker, and must not hold the parent back, or the count
could never reach zero. `launched` is not part of this count — it is the
person-facing record of the same fact the marker carries, and nothing reads it.

Two paths reach that count. The merged pull request is the primary one — a child's
delivery landing is what makes the question worth asking — and a person closing the
sub-issue by hand is the fallback, which skips itself when the closure already came
from a merge. Both write a marker tag on the parent before dispatching, so two
paths racing on the same child cannot start the atomaton twice.

If the parent has been closed meanwhile, nothing starts, and the notice says so
rather than retrying —

{"title": "Make the aggregation dispatch fail-closed on its own evidence", "reviewer": "reviewer", "body": "## What this changes

The aggregation gate already wrote an `atomaton:aggregated` marker before dispatching; the dispatch then posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Two comments said one thing, and the second was the run's ask.

**1. One comment per completion.** `dispatchRunner` now receives the marker's id as its `markerCommentId`, so the marker the gate already wrote is both the idempotency claim and the ask the run claims. Its body carries `DISPATCH_TAG` as well as `AGGREGATED_TAG`, which is not cosmetic: `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch`, and posts a separate claim for any other. Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. Now:

- no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;
- no marker **but** a caller-supplied ask (the runner's hand-off, whose result comment is the record) → still dispatched, check skipped, exactly as before.

The answers-request path posts no marker by design and is untouched — all its tests pass unchanged.

**3. The take-back, reasoned rather than guessed.** Because the marker is now the comment `dispatchRunner` was handed, its own `removeMarker` deletes it on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. The gate therefore no longer deletes it a second time: a 404 there was logged as "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry", which is the opposite of what happened. Only `failed` (GitHub rejecting the dispatch, marker still standing) reaches `takeBackMarker` now.

**4. One regression I introduced and then repaired.** `refused-closed` deliberately keeps the marker. Once the marker carries `atomaton:dispatch`, a closed parent would hold a standing request forever — `runInFlight` reads that as a run working or coming, and `prune_atomaton_data` would never prune the node. That is the shape #449 was made of. That branch now PATCHes the tag off, keeping the idempotency claim (`"aggregated"` is the true half) and dropping the promise.

`dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording was widened: it now covers both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible", instead of claiming GitHub hid the machinery's own marker.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Full `bun test` (after `bun run synth`, so `dist/` exists): **2202 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail**, 6671 expects, 176 files.
- New tests:
  - `src/app/aggregation.test.ts` — "an aggregation posts exactly one comment, and it is both the marker and the ask" (asserts exactly one `--method` write, both tags on it, `ask=777` on the dispatch); "a dispatch the thread cannot confirm is not sent, and the marker comes back" (no `workflow_dispatch`, exactly **one** DELETE of the marker); "a closed parent's marker keeps the aggregation claim and loses the dispatch tag".
  - `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts` — `describe("the dispatch's own evidence")`: marker POST fails + no ask → `unconfirmed`, no `workflow` call, notice posted; marker POST fails + caller's ask → `dispatched` with `ask=900`.
  - `src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` — first test rewritten to one POST rule (`atomaton:aggregated` → 556) and asserts exactly one write carrying both tags.

## Not done, deliberately

- No version bump, no release, no `docs/` change (nothing there describes the aggregation comment's shape), no `.github/**` or `dist/**` edit. `dist/` is gitignored and was only rebuilt so the generated-workflow tests could run.
"}

## スコープ(設計は決済済み。議論の余地があるのは手段のみ)

1. `aggregation.ts:344` の dispatch 呼び出しに `markerCommentId: markerId` を渡す。自前シード POST(`postDispatchMarker`)はこの経路から消える。

## What this changes

The aggregation gate already wrote an `atomaton:aggregated` marker before dispatching; the dispatch then posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Two comments said one thing, and the second was the run's ask.

**1. One comment per completion.** `dispatchRunner` now receives the marker's id as its `markerCommentId`, so the marker the gate already wrote is both the idempotency claim and the ask the run claims. Its body carries `DISPATCH_TAG` as well as `AGGREGATED_TAG`, which is not cosmetic: `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch`, and posts a separate claim for any other. Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. Now:

- no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;
- no marker **but** a caller-supplied ask (the runner's hand-off, whose result comment is the record) → still dispatched, check skipped, exactly as before.

The answers-request path posts no marker by design and is untouched — all its tests pass unchanged.

**3. The take-back, reasoned rather than guessed.** Because the marker is now the comment `dispatchRunner` was handed, its own `removeMarker` deletes it on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. The gate therefore no longer deletes it a second time: a 404 there was logged as "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry", which is the opposite of what happened. Only `failed` (GitHub rejecting the dispatch, marker still standing) reaches `takeBackMarker` now.

**4. One regression I introduced and then repaired.** `refused-closed` deliberately keeps the marker. Once the marker carries `atomaton:dispatch`, a closed parent would hold a standing request forever — `runInFlight` reads that as a run working or coming, and `prune_atomaton_data` would never prune the node. That is the shape #449 was made of. That branch now PATCHes the tag off, keeping the idempotency claim (`"aggregated"` is the true half) and dropping the promise.

`dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording was widened: it now covers both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible", instead of claiming GitHub hid the machinery's own marker.
